activity.notes: Cynane, daughter of Philip II, is not modeled as a sovereign. Her most consequential independent action was the armed expedition after Alexander's death to secure her daughter Adea-Eurydice's dynastic marriage. The event belongs around 323/322 BCE, so ATLAS uses an approximate military-activity window in Macedon.

sources.title: The Women of Alexander's Court - Cambridge Companion to Alexander the Great
sources.citation_text: The Cambridge Companion notes that Alexander's half-sister Cynnane became politically important after Alexander's death.

sources.title: A Mediterranean Game of Thrones - Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.citation_text: The Met describes Cynnane as a daughter of Philip II with battlefield experience who crossed into Asia with an armed force after Alexander's death.
